Thanks — reviewed the numbers. Short summary and recommended route: 

Summary of ask: 
- 3-year price umbrella (flat unit price years 1–3)
- Renewal smoothing: cap year-4 uplift at 8% if cumulative usage growth through year 3 <25%
- Projected committed volumes: 6B / 9B / 12B tokens (Y1/Y2/Y3)

Deal Desk assessment: 
- Commercially feasible with constraints. We should structure as: minimum annual committed spend + true-up; firm price umbrella conditioned on meeting a 75% annualized consumption threshold (reduces churn risk).
- Add an escalation clause: if realized aggregate utilization exceeds projections by >40% in any year, Redwood can request a mid-term uplift (with 60 days' notice) to maintain capacity economics.
- Renewal smoothing: recommend a 2-tier cap: 8% cap if growth <25%, 12% cap if growth between 25–50%. Above 50% we should treat as organic uplift and price per token resets to the then-current list price less agreed volume discounts.

Approvals needed: 
- Exec approval for price umbrella (exceptions to standard 12% annual uplift guard) — Aditya/Alex/Revenue execs
- Finance sign-off on revenue recognition treatment
- Legal to accept renewal language and mid-term uplift triggers

If leadership is okay with the 2-tier renewal cap and the utilization protection language above, I’ll draft the exact contract language for Legal. Requesting exec decision by EOD Friday (30 Oct) to keep Aureus momentum.

—Ben Carter\Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

Team — reviewed Ben’s recommendation and the attached volume model. I approve moving forward with the following guardrails for Aureus Health: 

1) Price umbrella: grant a flat unit price for years 1–3 conditioned on meeting the minimum annualized consumption threshold of 75% of committed volume per year.
2) Renewal smoothing (first renewal only): two-tier uplift cap — 8% cap if aggregate Y1–Y3 growth <25%; 12% cap if growth between 25–50%. If >50%, renewal resets to then-current list less volume discount schedule.
3) Mid-term utilization protection: allow Redwood to issue a capacity pricing adjustment (not retroactive) if realized utilization exceeds projections by >40% in any contract year; provide 60 days' notice and opportunity to work through capacity options before pricing adjustment.
4) Approval contingent on Finance confirming revenue recognition approach and Legal finalizing specific redlines to the renewal clause.

Tessa — please proceed to incorporate this language into the next draft and hand to Legal. Ben — thanks for the pragmatic tiers. Vivek — prep a capacity note in case they spike. Laura / Marcus — appreciate the candidness — we’re confident this keeps Aureus protected while letting Redwood manage economics.

Aditya Rao\VP, Revenue Operations\Redwood Inference
